title: Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 (fat grips review)
summary: NH reviews the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 fat grips he bought two years earlier, not for forearm training but to pad painfully thick metal dip bars and outdoor park bars. He praises their low price (under $20), flexibility and durability, notes they don't add much thickness, and warns they're easy to forget at the gym. He explains he plans programs years in advance and will only add fat grip training if his forearms stop growing.

claims.claim: He runs a program for years rather than months, spending hundreds of hours designing it, so he only adds new tools like fat grips when planned.
He will use fat grip training only as a last resort if his forearms refuse to grow; so far they are growing.
The Iron Bull Alpha Grips cost under $20 a pair, are very flexible and fit dumbbells, thick bars and dip bars.
He bought them because his old gym's thick metal dip bars dug into his large palms and hurt his wrists and hands; he also used them on outdoor park bars for pull-ups and dips.
After two years including outdoor use on rough equipment they show no wear; he recommends them (not affiliated).
They add only modest thickness; for extreme thickness choose another product.
Fat grips are easy to forget on a dumbbell in a commercial gym, so always pack them back in your bag.
